extract:
Meshuggah formed in Umeå, a university town in northern Sweden, in 1987, and have remained active ever since. They became one of the most influential extreme metal bands of their era. Guitarist Fredrik Thordendal had earlier played in a group that briefly used the Meshuggah name. He joined forces with vocalist Jens Kidman, and the lineup soon settled around Kidman, Thordendal, and drummer Tomas Haake, who arrived in 1990. Guitarist Mårten Hagström later joined, and Dick Lövgren became the long-term bassist in 2004. The name comes from a Yiddish word meaning crazy.

The band's early sound drew heavily on technical thrash in the vein of Metallica and other Bay Area acts. That influence is clear on their 1991 debut full-length, Contradictions Collapse, released through Nuclear Blast, the German label that has remained their home throughout their career. The 1994 EP None marked a turn toward the dense, syncopated, mid-tempo riffing that would define them. Destroy Erase Improve (1995) fused that approach with Thordendal's fluid, Allan Holdsworth-inspired lead playing, and it remains a touchstone release. The True Human Design EP (1997) bridged the gap to Chaosphere (1998), a colder and more relentless record anchored by tracks like New Millennium Cyanide Christ.

Nothing (2002) was where the band fully embraced down-tuned eight-string guitars and slower, polyrhythmic grooves. These patterns cycle against a steady 4/4 pulse, a technique that became their signature; Rational Gaze and Stengah are standout examples. In 2006 the album was reissued with re-recorded guitars. Catch Thirty Three (2005) took a radical step, presenting a single continuous composition built largely on programmed drums. ObZen (2008) returned to live drumming and produced Bleed, a track famous for Haake's punishing double-kick patterns and widely regarded as one of the most demanding drum performances in metal. Koloss (2012) leaned into heavier, groove-oriented material. The I EP, originally a single 21-minute piece from 2004, received a special edition reissue in 2014. Over these years the band also issued reissues and archival releases, including Rare Trax and the live documents Alive and The Ophidian Trek.

Meshuggah toured with acts such as Tool, whose members have publicly expressed admiration for them. Their precise, rhythmically displaced, palm-muted riffing gave rise to the term djent, an onomatopoeic description of that guitar tone. An entire movement followed, with bands like Periphery, Animals as Leaders, Tesseract, and Vildhjarta building on the template. Critics have consistently ranked Destroy Erase Improve, Nothing, and ObZen among the most important metal records of their respective decades. The band also earned Swedish Grammis nominations, and musicians across many genres cite them as a major influence on modern progressive and extreme metal.

Meshuggah continued after the period covered by those releases with The Violent Sleep of Reason (2016), recorded largely live in the studio, and Immutable (2022). Thordendal stepped back from touring in the late 2010s, with Per Nilsson filling in on stage. The band's legacy rests on reshaping how metal approaches rhythm. Their Umeå-born experiment in mechanical, mathematically intricate heaviness became the foundation for an entire subgenre.
title: Meshuggah
